rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī moves from signs within the self to signs across the horizons, where vegetation is the clearest created sign of resurrection.
rows.anchor: ونبه بآيات النفس ، فلم يبق إلا آيات الآفاق ، وكان النبات من آياتها أدل المخلوقات على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings forth pasture through rain from clouds, growing grass and other fodder for animals, both initially and again.
rows.anchor: بما أنزل من المعصرات فأنبت ما ترعاه الدواب من النجم وغيره بدءاً وإعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annual restoration of pasture after it fragments into soil proves resurrection: God can gather the dead from earth even more readily than renew plants.
rows.anchor: أقدر على جمع الأموات من الأرض بنفسه بعد أن تفتتوا من الماء على جمعه للنبات الذي كان تفتت في الأرض وصار تراباً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drying and darkening of grown greenery shows God's complete power and choice, bringing opposites together in one substance.
rows.anchor: ولما كان إيباسه وتسويده بعد اخضراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthāʾ means abundant plant matter, which dries, breaks apart, and is gathered by floodwater into froth, ruin, and fragments on the ground.
rows.anchor: أي بعد أطوار من زمن إخراجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥwā may describe vegetation saturated to blackish green, red tending to black, or green so intense that it tends toward black.
rows.anchor: حتى صار أسود يضرب إلى خضرة

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz defines ḥuwa as a horse-coat shade between black and chestnut; Biqāʿī says usage broadened until aḥwā could mean any black thing.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز رحمه الله في ديوانه : الحوة شية من شيات الخيل ، وهى بين الدهمة والكمتة ، وكثر هذا حتى سموا كل أسود أحوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also allows that the plant becomes black from severe drying, then winds gather its fragments from every direction.
rows.anchor: أنه أسود من شدة يبسه فحوته الرياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both terms carry senses of life and death; aḥwā comes second because its stronger association with green growth would otherwise constrain its sense.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يريد حينئذ أنه أسود من شدة يبسه فحوته الرياح وجمعته من كل أوب حيت تفتت ، فكل من الكلمتين فيها حياة وموت ، وأخر الثانية لتحملهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural dispositions have only fixed, necessary effects: fire burns what it touches and cannot then transform it into another quality; divine action can unite opposites.
rows.anchor: وأما الطبائع فليس لها من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pasture's yearly beginning and end recall resurrection; it is especially apt because cultivated growth crumbles to soil and God restores it with water just as He will restore the dead.
rows.anchor: وأشار بالبداية والنهاية إلى تذكر ذلك ، وأنه على سبيل التكرار في كل عام الدال على بعث الخلائق ، وخص المرعى لأنه أدل على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may will the Prophet to forget a passage because He has abrogated it, abrogating parts of the law according to benefits and easing the community's burden.
rows.anchor: ينسخ من الشريعة ما يشاء بحسب المصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God may make the greatest of creation forget a verse or word, displaying the Qur'an's majesty, then cause him to remember it again.
rows.anchor: أو لتظهر عظمته في أن أعظم الخلق يغلبه القرآن لأنه صفة الله فتنسى الآية أو الكلمة ثم تذكرها تارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet may remember what he forgot either when one of his community reminds him or through another means.
rows.anchor: فتنسى الآية أو الكلمة ثم تذكرها تارة بتذكير أحد من آحاد أمتك وتارة بغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to third person invokes the divine name, whose majesty is greater than explicit wording with an instrument of greatness.
rows.anchor: قال لافتاً القول إلى سياق الغيبة إعلاماً بأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The agent who recites and determines what may be forgotten must have encompassing knowledge; whatever God wills comes to pass, as 16:40 says.
rows.anchor: لا سيما الإقراء والحكم على ما يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in innahu signals God's exalted majesty, beyond creatures' hopes of comprehending Him amid His many acts.
rows.anchor: مؤكداً لأجل إنكار أهل القصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows aloud recitation and what is concealed, including private repetition in the Prophet's heart; both are equally known to Him.
rows.anchor: نسبة الجلي والخفي من جهره بالقرآن وترديده على قلبه سراً وغير ذلك إليه على حد سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The overt is named first because it is the discourse's focus; naming it does not restrict God's knowledge, and His knowledge of the hidden entails knowledge of it if disclosed.
rows.anchor: وأن نسبة الجلي والخفي من جهره بالقرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After discussing divinity, prophethood, and abrogation, Biqāʿī presents the revealed religion as tolerant and easy; what God establishes is easiest and most fitting for its time.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر الإلهيات والنبوة وأشير إلى النسخ ، أشار إلى أن الدين المشروع له هو الحنيفية السمحة ، وأنه سبحانه وتعالى لا يقيمه في شيء بنسخ أو غيره إلا كان هو الأيسر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the Prophet prepared, facilitated, gentle, and successful in the easy way, including preserving and contemplating revelation and every light, gentle course.
rows.anchor: أي في حفظ الوحي وتدبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording makes the Prophet himself easy and predisposed to love ease, rather than merely saying that God makes ease available for him.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لم يقل : ونيسر لك ، لأنه هو مطبوع على حبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites the saying that everyone is facilitated toward what they were created for as support for this divinely fitted ease.
rows.anchor: كل ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God completed and greatly eased the Prophet, he must remind everyone in every circumstance, compassionately completing others as God completed him.
rows.anchor: سبب عنه وجوب التذكير لكل أحد في كل حالة تكميلاً لغيره شفقة على خلق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has hours of spiritual breezes in which needs are fulfilled, giving the reminder an opportunity to benefit.
rows.anchor: فيها نفحات تقضى فيها الحاجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet resembles an accomplished physician treating the sick and benefits God's servants in gratitude for God's remembrance, by His permission.
rows.anchor: صار كالطبيب الحاذق في علاج المرضى فيقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī draws a lesson for disciples: a student needs the shaykhs' permission and purification, and must seek further good rather than rest content with what he has.
rows.anchor: أن يقتصر الإنسان على ما عنده ولا يطلب الازدياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional particle conveys universal scope: even a faintly hoped-for benefit warrants reminding, and the feminine verb signals that weak possibility.
rows.anchor: وعبر بأداة الشك إفهاماً للإطلاق الكلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people do not know the unseen, they cannot rule out benefit; the Prophet kept calling even in hardship and never despised or despaired of anyone.
rows.anchor: الغيب لا يقطع بعدم نفع أحد بل لا يزال على رجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commands to turn away from those who turn aside mean ceasing to grieve and wear oneself out in sorrow over them, not abandoning the reminder.
rows.anchor: الأمر بالإعراض عمن تولى ونحو ذلك إنما هو بالإعراض عن الحزن عليه ومن تقطيع النفس لأجله حسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People divide into those who accept treatment and those who do not; God has always known each group and individual but leaves them unspecified as a test, establishing proof by familiar means.
rows.anchor: إعلاماً بأنه سبحانه وتعالى عالم بكل من القسمين جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future form is a promise that cannot fail, extending even to the subtlest forms of reminder, as the assimilation suggests.
rows.anchor: أي بوعد لا خلف فيه ولو على أخفى وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who fears has some fear in his disposition and is destined for felicity: fear leads to good, acceptance, admonition, and lasting wholesome life in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وهو السعيد لما قدر له في نفسه من السعادة العظمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī's exhortation includes gratitude for gifts such as intellect and the faculties of the heart, tongue, and other limbs.
rows.anchor: حاثاً على شكر الجوائح من العقل ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love of God is marked by emulation; aversion for God's sake appears as avoidance, refraining, innovation, and refusal.
rows.anchor: وعلامة الحب الاقتداء ، وعلامة البغض التجنب والانتهاء والابتداع والإباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched person forces himself and his originally upright nature to avoid the reminder delivered by the noblest creature, closest to the Creator.
rows.anchor: أي يكلف نفسه وفطرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supreme wretch rejects the noblest messenger and so fears nothing; those who believe Muhammad are nobler than believers in earlier messengers.
rows.anchor: الذي له هذا الوصف على الإطلاق لأنه خالف أشرف الرسل فهو لا يخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma signals levels of the torment's extreme fluctuation between death and life whose height only God can know; no death recurs there, however long it lasts.
rows.anchor: فأشار إلى ذلك بالتعبير بأداة التراخي إعلاماً بأن مراتب هذه الشدة في التردد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To prevent non-death from sounding like an extraordinary honor, Biqāʿī clarifies that the person has no beneficial life because he was not purified, truthful, or prayerful.
rows.anchor: أي حياة تنفعه لأنه ما تزكى فلا صدق ولا صلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading addresses the audience directly, a shift signaling extreme anger; Abū ʿAmr retains third person, matching the prior context and its alternate inference.
rows.anchor: وبالغيب على الأصل عند أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuʾthirūn means choosing and privileging; worldly life is low, present, and perishable, yet people single it out for its immediacy.
rows.anchor: أي الدنية بالفناء الحاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sensory attachment occupies people's time like animals bound to what they perceive, keeping them from God's remembrance and self-purification and leaving them to appetite, sex, and wealth.
rows.anchor: كالحيوانات التي هي مقيدة بالمحسوسات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī casts this blame as the fourth treatment, purging vices by condemning what should be discarded and urging what should be acquired.
rows.anchor: بالذم على ما ينبغي البراءة منه والحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter is the exalted abode and the goal of creation and command; even conceding some good in this world, the next life is better because its bliss is wholly unspoiled.
rows.anchor: والحال أن الدار التي هي غاية الخلق ومقصود الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hereafter endures without end; even a worldly life prolonged to its eventual passing would only count as lasting figuratively, so perishable bliss cannot compare.
rows.anchor: على تقدير المحال في الدنيا من أن تماديها إلى وقت زوالها تسمى بقاء ، لأن نعيم الآخرة دائم لا انقطاع له أصلاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who knows this clear truth pursues the Hereafter and rejects both sensory worldly attractions and imagined pleasures of the lower self.
rows.anchor: اشتغل بما يحصل الآخرة وينفي الدنيا بقسميها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses fitting ellipsis: preferring and lowliness first imply leaving and elevation second, while goodness and permanence second imply their opposites first; the order first deters, then attracts.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الإيثار والدنو أولاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This means the great admonition of these sūras: glorification leading to purification through remembrance, prayer, turning from the world, and turning toward the Hereafter; it is the unalterable aim of every law.
rows.anchor: أي الوعظ العظيم بالتسبيح الذي ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ancient scriptures' long acceptance lends authority and makes souls more receptive; this confirms Muhammad follows earlier prophets' way, so an impartial person cannot single him out for rejection.
rows.anchor: ما مضت عليه السنون ومرت على قبوله الدهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an surpasses poets and soothsayers through eloquent praise, love poetry, heroic boasting, satire, exhortation, warning, narratives, and legal rulings, as well as reports of past and future unseen matters.
rows.anchor: فاستراح من ضلال الشعراء والكهان ، الموقعين في الإثم والعدوان

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Biqāʿī cites a hadith from Abū Dharr to support placing Abraham first because his scriptures are closer to admonition; he gives no grading.
rows.anchor: قدمه لأن صحفه أقرب إلى الوعظ كما نطق به حديث أبي ذر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is named last because his book is chiefly legal, with fewer admonitions; its forceful warnings include cursing Torah violators and foretelling their violation of its greatest glad tidings about Muhammad.
rows.anchor: الزواجر البليغة كاللعن لمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order also follows the prophets' chronology and precedence in virtue.
rows.anchor: مع أن ذكر النبيين عليهما الصلاة والسلام على الأصل في ترتيب الوجود والأفضلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazkiya means cleansing from impurities, attaining transcendence, and acquiring God's qualities to the extent possible.
rows.anchor: حث آخرها على التزكي وهو التطهر من الأدناس الذي هو معنى التنزه والتخلق بأخلاق الله بحسب الطاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding creation of purification shows God did not leave them without guidance or create them aimlessly; purposelessness is a grave imperfection from which He is exalted.
rows.anchor: إعلام بأن الله تعالى لم يهمل الخلق من البيان بعد أن خلقهم لأنه لم يخلقهم سدى ، لأن ذلك من العبث الذي هو من أكبر النقائص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra's ending returns to its beginning: glorifying God and purifying the soul together form its central purpose.
rows.anchor: فقد رجع آخرها على أولها ، وكان تنزيه الرب سبحانه وتعالى وتنزيه النفس أيضاً غاية معولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wonders of creation prove God's complete power, including resurrection and all promised events in Paradise and Hell, so people should contemplate them and follow the messenger.
rows.anchor: على البعث وعلى كل ما ذكر أنه يفعله في الجنة والنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remind everyone who might benefit by appealing to innate knowledge that creation confirms revelation and divine power; do not be distressed when people fail to reflect, since reminding may awaken them.
rows.anchor: كل من يرجى تذكره وانتفاعه بالتذكير يا أشرف خلقنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī offers inward correspondences: obedient camels resemble tranquil souls, the sky luminous spirits, mountains stable intellects and knowledge, and earth the body with its organs.
rows.anchor: أن الإبل تشبه الأنفس المطمئنة الذلولة المطيعة المناقدة ، والسماء تشبه الأرواح القدسية النورانية ، والجبال تشبه العقول والمعارف الثابتة الراسخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because this is an early Meccan sūra when the Prophet was commanded to forbear, he is a reminder, not a fighter or coercive enforcer; he is responsible only for conveying the message.
rows.anchor: فلا عليك إن لم ينظروا ولم يتذكروا لأنه ما عليك إلا البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'over them' restricts the Prophet's lack of control to those people; the preposition conveys domination.
rows.anchor: وأشار إلى القهر بأداة الاستعلاء فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muṣayṭir means one who dominates or controls; Biqāʿī adds that God will soon grant the Prophet authority over others.
rows.anchor: وأما غيرهم فسنسلطك عليهم عن قريب

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the word with sīn, following its original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأها الكسائي بالسين على الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell cannot move itself, since that might suggest it lies beyond God's power; angels lead it, and their handling of it creates overwhelming terror.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت جهنم لا تأتي بنفسها لأنها لو أتت بنفسها لربما ظن أنها خارجة عن القدرة بل تقودها الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Biqāʿī reports without naming an authority or grading that Hell is brought with seventy thousand reins, each held by seventy thousand angels.
rows.anchor: روي أنه يؤتى بها لها سبعون ألف زمام مع كل زمام سبعون ألف ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links Hell's being brought forth to 79:36, where Gehenna is exposed to sight.
rows.anchor: { وبرزت الجحيم لمن يرى }[ النازعات : 36 ]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated yawmidhin is an appositive clarifying the earlier temporal phrase after a long interval, heightening dread as people see what is prepared for the thankful and ungrateful.
rows.anchor: توضيحاً لطول الفصل وتهويلاً قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only then does a person continually remember what benefited or harmed him and see worldly love brought loss: it neither gained what was not allotted nor made him lose what was allotted by giving it up.
rows.anchor: فيذكر كل ما كان ينفعه في الدنيا وما يضره فيعلم أن حبه للدنيا لم يفده إلا خساراً ، لا زاد بحبها شيئاً لم يكتب له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance cannot benefit him then because the Hereafter is no longer a place for deeds; it yields only regret, multiplied grief, anxiety, and pain.
rows.anchor: فإنه في غير موضعه ، فلا ينفعه أصلاً بوجه من الوجوه لفوات دار العمل ، ولا يقع بذلك على شيء سوى الندم وتضاعف الغم والهم والآلام
